posts.author: DevRPG2k

You really need to use a bit more imagination to get around these problems.
For example, I think in 2013 I made a menu using maps, the item reading and status were all done with variables, which could be reused in other maps so as not to have to recreate the same calculations that separated the decimal places several times.
I wasn't the first, several others had already done this, at the time I just did it to leave it as something easy for others to study:
See, all done in one map:
Here's how simple it is to create a healing item that is removed after use:
This is a menu for a single character in the Party, making this menu for more characters in the Party would require a lot of modifications.
It is worth remembering that this is an example, I advise you to create your own, try it out instead of just following the steps, knowledge comes with trial and error.

Because variables change
Is this a question or a statement?
If it is a statement, it is viable, because an event on the map can return to 0 when it enters and leaves the map.
If it is a question, the variable changes, keeping a fixed number is the secret to keeping everything organized, when you save the game and enter, all your variables will be there numbered and fixed. Equating a variable to another variable prevents change, allows control over the number.
So what is the most important thing to fix on the map? What are the elements that undergo changes?

posts.author: Eternidade_1
posts.body:
Sorry if I was arrogant. I didn't know the term "functional menu simulator".
A custom menu is hard to make, it's like having a game within the game, you'll have to create everything, items, skills, equipment, status, enemies, battle systems, among other things that are part of the normal standard menu.
There are several ways to get a custom menu, via scripts or plugins, but with events it's more complicated.
I tried a few times to reproduce mode 7 through events and I couldn't. My event menu originated from a Mog script that had a custom menu at the time for vx ace.
Then I realized that I could create it through events, and that was it.
Many factors must be taken into account in the menu, such as the acquisition of new items, skills or equipment, which may or may not have a direct connection to the database.
I have Rpg Maker 2k, Xp and MV installed on my PC, but I don't know if the menu would work correctly in 2k.
